f. Discharge from the unit may occur after completion of all procedures on Day 9 and on Day 40 and after the Investigator has reviewed all safety assessment (including safety laboratory tests) and confirmed that the participant is appropriate for discharge.

g. A single outpatient visit or phone call and safety laboratory assessment should occur between Day 14 and Day 18. A phone call may take place on a different day than the blood draw within the Day 14 through Day 18 period.
h. If needed to confirm menopause.
i. Parameters include age and sex. Race and ethnicity will be collected where permitted by local regulations.
j. Wilson disease history will include diagnosis date, method of diagnosis, history of cirrhosis, details of any previous liver biopsies performed, and treatment received.

k. A full physical examination will be performed at Screening, at check_in for the study, and at the End of the study/Early Termination Visit. A physical examination should also be performed on any participants with ongoing adverse events prior to discharge from the unit. Otherwise, a symptom_driven physical examination may be performed at other times, at the Principal Investigator's discretion.
l. Height at screening only.

m. While in the CRU, study intervention will be administered after an overnight fast (ie, at least 10 hours) at the same time every morning; drug is to be administered with 240 mL of water and meals should be delayed a minimum of 2 hours after dosing. As an outpatient, participants are expected to take ALXN1840 at approximately the same time daily (+/_1 hour). Participants should take the medication with a glass of water on an empty stomach; meals should be delayed a minimum of 2 hours after dosing.
n. During the outpatient period, participants will use SMS text messaging to confirm study intervention administration.
o. Blood sampling for PK/PD will occur before ALXN1840 administration and represents a predose trough. See Table 2 for PK/PD sampling on Days 1, 25, 29, and 39.
p. PK/PD collection will include timepoints described in the schedule of PK/PD assessment for Days 1, 25, 29, and 39 (Table 2).

q. Samples for serum chemistry will be obtained following a fast of at least 8 hours at the Screening Visit and at check_in. In case of rechecks, and postdose serum chemistry, participants may not have fasted for 6 or 8 hours before the serum chemistry sample is taken.
r. Laboratory assessment including chemistry, hematology, and coagulation parameters should be performed on Days _8, _1, 8, 23, and 28 only.

s. Menstruation check for women only; women of childbearing potential should only be enrolled after a negative serum pregnancy test result at Screening. Additional urine pregnancy testing will be standard for the protocol unless serum testing is required by site policies, local regulation, or Institutional Review Boards (IRBs)/Independent Ethics Committees (IECs) (Section 10.2). In addition to pregnancy tests detailed at the visits in the SoA, females of childbearing potential will be required to perform urine pregnancy tests at least every 4 weeks at their home or the study site throughout their time in the study.
t. A single 15 mL serum sample will be retained for evaluation in the event of an unexpected safety finding; retained samples may be destroyed after completion of the clinical study report.

u. Vital signs measurements and ECGs should be performed predose, unless otherwise specified. Vitals signs include body temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, and systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

v. Copper_ and molybdenum_controlled diet will be initiated after registration/inclusion. Participants will remain on a copper/molybdenum controlled diet throughout both the inpatient Period 1 (Day _8 to Day 9) and inpatient Period 2 (Day 23 to Day 40); during this time participants will be strongly encouraged to complete all meals. While not in the CRU, participants will be encouraged to adhere to their usual copper_controlled diet.
w. For each input/output balance period, 24_hour urine samples are to be collected for measurement of copper and molybdenum.
x. For fecal samples, each individual sample will be independently collected with record of date, time, and weight of the sample.

data.text: In the event that items cannot be accurately quantified, items may be balanced during pretreatment period and post_treatment period to support the change from baseline assessment.
Participants will be strongly encouraged to void within 2 hours of completion of each 24_hour period (ie, dosing time).

To ensure flexibility, the Outpatient Period during Treatment Period 1 may be extended up to an additional 14 days with Investigator approval. In such cases, the actual Outpatient Period duration will be recorded and the participant will continue Inpatient Period 2 at Day 23.
At the CRU's discretion, participants may remain in the CRU during the outpatient period for safety or to maintain the integrity of the conduct of the study.

This study incorporates the use of an adaptive design. Adaptive features may be implemented at the discretion of the Investigator to support conduct of the study. Such adaptive features do not require amendment of the protocol.
Dose range limit 15 mg every other day to 30 mg/day; Outpatient Period extension not >14 days; check_in to clinical research unit allowed 1 day prior.

Acetaminophen should be limited to 1000 mg/day. Herbal remedies must be discontinued at least 7 days prior to first admission until study completion. Over_the_counter medications may be given if they are not expected to impact the outcome of the study.

If the study intervention is definitively discontinued, the participant should remain in the study to be evaluated for safety follow_up.
This review of the ECG printed at the time of collection must be documented. Any new clinically relevant finding should be reported as an AE.

Blood pressure and heart rate measurements should be preceded by at least 5 minutes of rest for the participant in a quiet setting without distractions (eg, television, cell phones). Ideally, the same arm for each participant should be used for measurements.

If vital signs are abnormal as defined by inclusion/exclusion criteria, 2 additional vital signs measurements will be made. The average of the 3 vital signs measurements will be recorded in the CRF and used to determine participant eligibility.
As with vital signs, if ECG interval measurements are abnormal, an additional triplicate will be performed and recorded in the CRF.

All laboratory tests with values considered abnormal and clinically significant during participation in the study or after the last dose of study intervention should be repeated until the values return to normal or baseline or are no longer considered clinically significant by the Investigator or Medical Monitor.

All SAEs will be recorded and reported to Alexion or the designee immediately and under no circumstance should this exceed 24 hours, as indicated in Section 10.3. The Investigator will submit any updated SAE data to Alexion within 24 hours of it being available.

data.text: There are no adverse events of special interest for this study.

A single biobanked serum sample will be collected predose from each participant to serve as a retained sample during the study. Samples will remain on site and will be discarded following the completion of the clinical study report. The sample will not be used for genetic testing (see Section 8.7).

For this study, any dose of ALXN1840 greater than that specified in the protocol will be considered an overdose. Overdoses are medication errors that are not considered AEs unless there is an untoward medical occurrence resulting from the overdose.
Samples collected within ± 10% or 30 min, whichever is less, of the scheduled time will not be considered a protocol deviation.

Excess/additional samples may be stored for up to 5 years and used for PD and/or diagnostic biomarker development and research to understand the pathways associated with the mechanism of action of ALXN1840. These samples will not be used for genetic analyses (ie, RNA or DNA analyses). Genetic analyses will not be performed on these whole blood samples. Participant confidentiality will be maintained.
Genetics will not be evaluated in this study.
Immunogenicity Assessments: Not applicable.
Health economic and medical resource utilization parameters are not evaluated in this study.

data.name: Contraceptive requirements
data.text: Contraceptive use by men or women should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies. a. Male participants: Male participants, if heterosexually active and with a female spouse or partner of childbearing potential or a pregnant or breastfeeding spouse or partner, must agree to use barrier contraception (male condom) for the duration of the study and for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Male participants must not donate sperm for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Female spouses or partners of male participants who are of childbearing potential must use highly effective contraception as defined below and in Section 10.4, starting at least 1 menstrual cycle before (the male participant's) first study intervention administration and continuing until at least 3 months after the end of their male partner's systemic exposure to the study intervention. Barrier contraception (male condom) is required even with documented medical assessment of surgical success of a vasectomy. For male participants who have had a vasectomy (with documented evidence of azoospermia if possible) and agree to use a male condom for the stated time period, no additional contraceptive method is required by their female partner. b. Female participants: Female participants or female partners of male participants of childbearing potential (including breastfeeding females), if heterosexually active, must be willing to follow protocol_specified contraception guidance starting at least 1 menstrual cycle before first study intervention administration and continuing for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Female participants must not donate ova for at least 3 months after the end of systemic exposure of the study intervention. Female participants who are documented as being of non_childbearing potential as defined in Section 10.4 are exempt from contraception requirements. Highly effective contraceptive methods for female participants and female partners of male participants are described in Section 10.4.

data.name: Primary Estimand _ Net Copper Balance with ALXN1840 15 mg and 30 mg
data.populationSummary: Adult participants with confirmed Wilson disease meeting all eligibility criteria, admitted to a clinical research unit on a copper_controlled diet, previously treated with chelator therapy (discontinued approximately 4 days prior to Day 1) and off zinc therapy for at least 21 days (Full Analysis Set (all enrolled participants who received at least 1 dose of ALXN1840 and have evaluable copper intake/output collections); no comparator arm (single_arm, open_label, within_participant dose comparison)) Summary measure: Descriptive summary statistics (n, arithmetic mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of mean daily copper balance by dose level and collection period, with proportion of participants achieving net negative copper balance.

intercurrentEvents.text: ALXN1840 dose is decreased (to as low as 15 mg every other day) or interrupted because dose modification criteria are met; all available copper balance data are analyzed as observed under the actual dose administered

Enrollment Definition
data.description: Definition of an enrolled participant
data.text: 'Enrolled' means all participants who sign the informed consent form (ICF), are eligible for the study, and are registered on Day _7 when participants are assigned a participant number.

data.name: SRC Safety Review Before Dose Titration
data.description: Safety Review Committee gating condition for up_titration to 30 mg/day
data.text: Before titration to 30 mg/day, the Safety Review Committee (SRC) will review available safety data through Day 23 for each participant.

data.name: Safety Concern Precluding Dose Escalation
data.description: Condition under which participants remain at 15 mg/day
data.text: Dosing initiated at 15 mg once daily for a minimum of 4 weeks with an increase to 30 mg after 4 weeks, unless there are safety concerns that, in the opinion of the Investigator(s) and/or Alexion, may place participants at undue risk, in which case participants may remain on the 15 mg/day dose for the duration of the study.

data.name: Outpatient Period Extension Condition
data.description: Conditions for extending the Outpatient Period during Treatment Period 1
data.text: To ensure flexibility, the Outpatient Period during Treatment Period 1 may be extended up to an additional 14 days with Investigator approval. Participants will be given additional investigational product to support daily dosing throughout the Outpatient Period; the actual Outpatient Period duration will be recorded and the participant will continue Inpatient Period 2 at Day 23.

data.name: Retention in CRU During Outpatient Period
data.description: Condition permitting continued inpatient stay instead of discharge on Day 9
data.text: At the CRU's discretion, participants may remain in the CRU during the outpatient period for their own safety or to maintain the integrity of the conduct of the study.

data.name: Adaptive Design Features
data.description: Adaptive design condition permitting protocol_independent operational changes
data.text: This study incorporates the use of an adaptive design. Adaptive features may be implemented at the discretion of the Investigator to support conduct of the study. Such adaptive features do not require amendment of the protocol. Adaptive features and their limits are described in Table 4.

data.name: Zinc Washout Condition
data.description: Requirement to be off zinc therapy before first dose
data.text: To prevent confounding of the study results, participants must be off zinc therapy for a minimum of 21 days prior to Day 1; the inhibitory effect of zinc on intestinal copper absorption is expected to be minimal 21 days after discontinuation of zinc.

data.name: Chelator Discontinuation for Baseline Assessment
data.description: Condition for pretreatment copper baseline measurement
data.text: To assess the copper baseline during the Inpatient Run_in Period, participants will be discontinued from their chelator therapy for approximately 4 days prior to initiating ALXN1840, while maintained on a copper_controlled diet.

data.name: Women of Childbearing Potential Enrollment Condition
data.description: Pregnancy testing eligibility condition
data.text: Women of childbearing potential should only be enrolled after a negative serum pregnancy test result at Screening; females of childbearing potential must perform urine pregnancy tests at least every 4 weeks throughout their time in the study.

data.name: Dietary Compliance Condition
data.description: Willingness to comply with controlled diet
data.text: Participants unwilling to consistently complete every meal and tolerate a controlled, limited menu for the duration of the study are excluded.

data.name: Hepatic Dose Modification Criterion
data.description: Hepatic laboratory trigger requiring temporary interruption
data.text: Bilirubin > 2 × ULN accompanied by ALT > 3 × ULN, indicative of liver injury: temporary interruption of ALXN1840 with weekly repeat testing.

data.name: Hematologic Dose Modification Criterion
data.description: Neutrophil decline trigger requiring dose reduction
data.text: > 30% decrease from baseline in neutrophils with neutrophils below reference range at baseline: reduce dose to previous dose level if up_titration has occurred, or reduce to 15 mg QOD if on 15 mg QD; no further dose increase until resolution of abnormality; weekly repeat testing.

data.name: Neurological Worsening Criterion
data.description: Neurologic safety assessment trigger
data.text: Evidence of neurologic worsening by AEs or by neurologic physical exam assessment: Investigator and Alexion Medical Monitor will evaluate the need for dose modification (interruption, increase or decrease) based on copper control parameters and relevant clinical data; rationale must be documented and re_evaluated at the next study visit.

data.name: Psychiatric Worsening Criterion
data.description: Psychiatric safety assessment trigger
data.text: Evidence of clinically significant acute psychiatric worsening which may include but is not limited to suicidality, acute depression, or psychosis: Investigator and Alexion Medical Monitor will evaluate the need for dose modification (interruption, increase or decrease).

data.name: Rechallenge Conditions
data.description: Conditions for rechallenge after dose interruption
data.text: A maximum of 3 rechallenges will be allowed. Rechallenge after bilirubin elevation is at 15 mg QOD or less frequent when bilirubin is below ULN and requires approval of the Alexion Medical Monitor. Participants who were on 15 mg QOD should be rechallenged at the 15 mg QOD dose. The Investigator, in consultation with the Medical Monitor, may change dose and dose frequency in participants who require rechallenge.

data.name: Clinically Significant ECG/QTcF Finding
data.description: Post_enrollment clinically significant finding evaluation
data.text: If a clinically significant finding is identified (including, but not limited to, changes from baseline in QTcF) after enrollment, the Investigator or qualified designee will determine if the participant can continue in the study and if any change in participant management is needed.

data.name: Lost to Follow_up Condition
data.description: Definition and required contact attempts
data.text: A participant will be considered lost to follow_up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site. Before being deemed lost to follow_up, the Investigator or designee must make every effort to regain contact (where possible, 3 telephone calls and, if necessary, a certified letter to the last known mailing address).

data.name: Concomitant Ibuprofen Limit
data.description: Dose limit condition for permitted concomitant CYP2C9 substrate
data.text: Ibuprofen dose must not exceed 1200 mg in any 24_hour period and may only be used with approval of the Investigator; paracetamol/acetaminophen maximum 1000 mg per day permitted with Investigator approval.

data.name: Screening_Only Site Condition (US)
data.description: Operational condition applicable only in the US
data.text: Sites in the US may only perform screening procedures and not any of the remaining study procedures, to facilitate participant recruitment across different regions of the US.

data.name: Screening to Run_in (Enrollment) Transition
data.text: Participants eligible for the study will be enrolled on Day _7 (registered and assigned a participant number) and initiated on a copper_ and molybdenum_controlled diet; participants are admitted to the CRU on Day _8. Women of childbearing potential may only be enrolled after a negative serum pregnancy test at Screening.

data.name: Run_in to Treatment Period 1 Transition
data.text: Following the Run_in Period (diet equilibration Day _7 to Day _5 and baseline copper/molybdenum balance collection Day _4 to Day _1), participants will be administered ALXN1840 15 mg/day beginning on Day 1. Participants must be off zinc therapy for a minimum of 21 days prior to Day 1 and off chelator therapy for approximately 4 days prior to Day 1.

data.name: Inpatient Period 1 to Outpatient Period Transition
data.text: Participants may be discharged from the CRU on Day 9 (after completion of Day 1_8 intake/output collection) or remain in the CRU for their own safety or to maintain the integrity of the conduct of the study. During the Outpatient Period participants confirm study intervention administration via SMS text messaging.

data.name: Outpatient Period to Inpatient Period 2 Transition
data.text: Participants who were discharged will be re_admitted to the CRU on Day 22 or Day 23 (predose); all procedures will start on Day 23 and participants remain in house until Day 40. If the Outpatient Period was extended (up to an additional 14 days with Investigator approval), the participant will continue Inpatient Period 2 at Day 23.

data.name: Dose Escalation to 30 mg/day on Day 29
data.text: Following approximately 28 days at 15 mg/day, participants are titrated up to 30 mg/day on Day 29. Before titration, the SRC will review available safety data through Day 23 for each participant. Escalation will not occur if there are safety concerns that, in the opinion of the Investigator(s) and/or Alexion, may place the participant at undue risk, in which case the participant may remain on 15 mg/day for the duration of the study.

data.name: Dose Reduction for Hematologic Toxicity
data.text: > 30% decrease from baseline in neutrophils with neutrophils below reference range at baseline: reduce dose to the previous dose level if up_titration has occurred, or reduce dose to 15 mg QOD if on 15 mg QD. No further dose increase until resolution of the abnormality, with weekly repeat testing.

data.name: Temporary Dosing Interruption for Hepatic Injury
data.text: Bilirubin > 2 × ULN accompanied by ALT > 3 × ULN indicative of liver injury requires temporary interruption of ALXN1840 with weekly repeat testing; rechallenge at 15 mg QOD or less frequent when bilirubin is below ULN and only with approval of the Alexion Medical Monitor.

data.name: Dose Modification for Neurological or Psychiatric Worsening
data.text: For evidence of neurologic worsening (AEs or neurologic physical exam) or clinically significant acute psychiatric worsening (including suicidality, acute depression, or psychosis), the Investigator and Alexion Medical Monitor will evaluate the need for dose modification (interruption, increase, or decrease) based on copper control parameters and relevant clinical data; rationale must be documented and re_evaluated at the next study visit.

data.name: Rechallenge After Dose Interruption
data.text: A maximum of 3 rechallenges will be allowed. Participants who were on 15 mg QOD should be rechallenged at the 15 mg QOD dose. The Investigator, in consultation with the Medical Monitor, may change dose and dose frequency in participants who require rechallenge. Deviation from dose modification guidelines must be agreed with the Alexion Medical Monitor.

data.name: Discontinuation of Study Intervention for Safety/Compliance Events
data.text: Participants must be considered for discontinuation from study intervention if any of the following occur: serious hypersensitivity reaction; severe uncontrolled infection; use of disallowed medication; pregnancy or planned pregnancy; or Alexion or the Investigator deems it necessary for the participant. Investigators must notify Alexion immediately of study intervention discontinuation; the decision should not be delayed for causality assessment.

data.name: Discontinuation of Study Intervention for Abnormal Liver Function
data.text: Discontinuation of study intervention for abnormal liver function should be considered by the Investigator when a participant meets one of the conditions outlined in the Dose Modification criteria (Section 6.6) or if the Investigator believes it is in the best interest of the participant.

data.name: Continuation in Study After Intervention Discontinuation
data.text: If the study intervention is definitively discontinued, the participant should remain in the study to be evaluated for safety follow_up, with data collected per the Schedule of Activities at the time of discontinuation and follow_up.

data.name: Post_Study Therapy Transition
data.text: Following completion of both inpatient periods of the study (ie, Day 40), participants will either transition to therapy that was discontinued before enrollment, transition to other standard of care therapy as directed by the treating physician, or, at the discretion of the treating physician, request continuation of ALXN1840 treatment permissible under local regulations for preapproval access. All participants should return to the CRU for the EOS Visit on Day 54 (+/_ 2 days).

data.name: Participant Withdrawal at Own Request or Investigator Discretion
data.description: A participant may withdraw from the study at any time at his/her own request, or may be withdrawn at any time at the discretion of the Investigator for safety, behavioral, compliance, or administrative reasons. The reason must be recorded in source documents and the CRF, and the participant is permanently discontinued from both study intervention and the study at that time.

data.name: Early Termination/Early Discontinuation Visit
data.description: At the time of discontinuation from the study, if possible, an early discontinuation visit (EOS/ET Visit) should be conducted as shown in the SoA, including a full physical examination and collection of specified samples and data.

data.name: Lost to Follow_up Exit
data.description: Should the participant continue to be unreachable after documented contact attempts (where possible, 3 telephone calls and, if necessary, a certified letter), he/she will be considered to have withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: A participant is considered to have completed the study if he/she has completed all phases of the study including the last scheduled procedure shown in the Schedule of Activities (EOS Visit on Day 54 +/_ 2 days). The end of the study is defined as the date the last participant completes the last visit shown in the SoA.

data.name: Study or Site Termination by Sponsor or Investigator
data.description: Alexion reserves the right to close the study site or terminate the study at any time for any reason. Reasons for early closure may include failure of the Investigator to comply with the protocol, IRB/IEC or local health authority requirements, Alexion's procedures or GCP guidelines; inadequate recruitment of participants; or discontinuation of further study intervention development. If prematurely terminated or suspended, Alexion shall promptly inform Investigators, IECs/IRBs, and regulatory authorities, and the Investigator shall inform participants and assure appropriate therapy and/or follow_up.

data.name: Pregnancy Exit from Study Intervention
data.description: Pregnancy or planned pregnancy requires the participant to be considered for discontinuation of study intervention.

data.name: SRC Safety Review Decision Prior to Dose Titration
data.description: Before titration to 30 mg/day on Day 29, the Safety Review Committee reviews available safety data through Day 23 for each participant to determine whether up_titration may proceed.

data.name: Day 9 Discharge Decision
data.description: Decision whether the participant is discharged from the CRU on Day 9 to the Outpatient Period or remains in the CRU for safety or study conduct integrity.

data.name: Outpatient Period Extension Decision
data.description: Investigator decision to extend the Outpatient Period during Treatment Period 1 by up to an additional 14 days, with provision of additional investigational product; participant continues Inpatient Period 2 at Day 23.

data.name: Day 29 Dose Escalation Decision
data.description: Decision to increase dose from 15 mg/day to 30 mg/day on Day 29, or to maintain 15 mg/day for the duration of the study if safety concerns exist.

data.name: Laboratory_Based Dose Modification Decision
data.description: Assessment of hepatic (bilirubin/ALT) and hematologic (neutrophil) laboratory parameters against dose modification criteria at scheduled (Days _8, _1, 8, 23, 28) and weekly repeat testing, triggering dose reduction, interruption, or restriction of dose increases.

data.name: Neurologic/Psychiatric Assessment Decision
data.description: Investigator and Alexion Medical Monitor decision on dose modification (interruption, increase, or decrease) based on evidence of neurologic or acute psychiatric worsening, copper control parameters, and relevant clinical data; re_evaluated at the next study visit.
